## What happens

`scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py <change> --revision <abbreviated-sha>` compares the
caller's `--revision` string against the change's full `current_revision` and, because
an abbreviation never equals a full SHA, refuses with a staleness error naming two
SHAs that are visibly the same commit:

```
$ python scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py 3149 --revision bed4448e175
refusing stale submit: inspected bed4448e175, current is bed4448e175bb0b7c28fce7d22ab673d65cfadec
```

Observed 2026-10-30 submitting Gerrit 3149. Re-running with the full 40-character SHA
submitted successfully, so the change was never stale.

## Why it matters

The message asserts a condition that is false. It names the guard's real purpose —
"another session uploaded a newer revision" — in a case where no such upload happened,
so the obvious reading is that a concurrent session raced you. The correct response
(re-run with a longer SHA) is not discoverable from the output, and the incorrect
response (re-poll, re-push, or investigate a phantom race) costs a vote cycle.

Abbreviated SHAs are the natural input here: `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, `git log
--oneline`, and the `%h` format all produce them, and every other `git` command in the
landing workflow accepts them.

## Root cause

The full 40-character requirement is deliberate and stays: `_revision_matches` requires
`len(inspected) == 40`, `tests/unit/test_gerrit_submit_if_current_8b1c.py::test_safe_submit_refuses_abbreviated_revision_prefix`
asserts that a prefix of the current revision is refused with exit 2, and AGENTS.md,
CONTRIBUTING.md §2e and docs/releasing.md all document `--revision <current-full-sha>`.
The defect is only the message: `main` routes every `_revision_matches` failure,
including a value that is not a full SHA at all, to the "refusing stale submit" branch.
That conflates "the revision you named is not in the required form" with "the revision
you named is no longer current".

## Approach

In `scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py`, validate the form of `--revision` before comparing it
with the change: it must be exactly 40 hexadecimal characters (case-insensitive). When it
is not, print a distinct refusal on stderr that says a full 40-character commit SHA is
required, echoes the value given, and tells the operator how to get one
(`git rev-parse HEAD`), with no staleness wording, and return exit 2 (unchanged, so the
existing exit-code contract and docstring hold; the docstring's exit-2 line gains this
case). The form check runs before any Gerrit request, so a malformed value is refused
without network access and without reading the change. A well-formed full SHA that differs
from `current_revision` keeps the existing "refusing stale submit" message and exit 2.
The comparison logic itself (`_revision_matches`) is unchanged; prefixes stay refused.

## Scope

- `scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py` — form validation + distinct message; docstring exit-2 note.
- `tests/unit/test_gerrit_submit_if_current_8b1c.py` — test updates below.
- No doc change: AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md/docs/releasing.md already say full SHA.

Out of scope: accepting abbreviated SHAs (rejected design), and the HTTP 409 reporting path
(`_explain_409`), which this change must not alter.

## Testing

All in `tests/unit/test_gerrit_submit_if_current_8b1c.py`, with `_credential`/`_request`
stubbed (no network):

- `test_safe_submit_refuses_abbreviated_revision_prefix` keeps its exit-2 / no-submit
  assertions and additionally asserts stderr says a full 40-character SHA is required,
  mentions `git rev-parse HEAD`, and does not contain "stale".
- New parametrized malformed-input case (e.g. 40 chars with a non-hex character, 41 hex
  chars, empty string): exit 2, no Gerrit request issued, distinct message, no "stale".
- `test_safe_submit_refuses_stale_revision_before_submit` changes its inputs to two
  different well-formed 40-character SHAs and still asserts "refusing stale submit"
  (today it passes an 8-character value, which under this design is a form error).
- Existing full-SHA success and 409 tests stay green unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** `gerrit_safe_submit.py <n> --revision <abbreviated sha>` exits 2, submits
  nothing, and prints a message stating a full 40-character commit SHA is required and
  naming `git rev-parse HEAD`; the output contains no "stale" wording.
- [x] **AC2** A malformed `--revision` (non-hex character, wrong length) gets the same
  distinct refusal and exit 2 without any Gerrit request.
- [x] **AC3** A well-formed full SHA that differs from `current_revision` still prints
  "refusing stale submit" and exits 2.
- [x] **AC4** The full current 40-character SHA on a green change still submits, exit 0.
- [x] **AC5** Unit tests cover AC1–AC4 with stubbed Gerrit responses and no network access.
- [x] **AC6** `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, and the change is `Verified +1` in CI.
